images.title: Five coconut halves
images.purpose: Show that five halves pair up into two wholes with one half left: 5/2 = 2 + 1/2.
images.composition: A top row of five loose halves and, below it, the same halves regrouped as two whole coconuts and one half, with wide space between rows.
images.exact_structure: Top row: exactly 5 identical coconut halves drawn as plain flat half circles, evenly spaced, outline only. A thin grey #6B7280 arrow points down. Bottom row: exactly 2 whole coconuts, each made of 2 halves joined along a visible line, filled teal #0072B2; then exactly 1 single half filled amber #E69F00, set slightly apart. All 10 halves in the frame are the same size. Exactly 2 rows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a photographic or textured coconut, or halves of different sizes
images.takeaway: Five halves is two wholes and one half more.
images.description: A row of 5 coconut halves labelled 5/2; below, they pair into 2 teal whole coconuts with 1 amber half left, labelled 5/2 = 2 + 1/2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to pair the halves in the top row and say how many wholes and how much is left.

image_decisions.why: Regrouping five halves into wholes is clearest as a before and after picture.
